question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}x, & \,1\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}{y}^{2}, & \,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 1.5,Y\ge 1).$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}x\cdot \frac{3}{8}{y}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [1,2]\times [0,2].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{2}, & \,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1.5,Y\ge 1) & ={\int }_{1}^{1.5}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{1.5}\frac{1}{4}x{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{1.5}\frac{1}{4}x(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{1.5}\frac{7}{12}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{7{x}^{2}}{24}]}_{1}^{1.5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{7(1.5)^{2}}{24}-\frac{7(1)^{2}}{24} \\  & ≈0.365.\end{aligned}
$$
